svg.title: From Minecraft video to a position estimate
svg.desc: Sixteen images enter a frozen video encoder. Activations from three blocks are spatially averaged into separate 1024-number feature vectors. A separate ridge probe estimates endpoint position. Recorded coordinates train and evaluate only the probe, never the encoder.
svg.text: What the model sees — and what we measure
Proposed extraction pipeline • schematic, not experimental results
1. Take 16 Minecraft images
Every 8 simulation ticks • endpoint = the last image
2. Prepare the images
Mask bottom 12% HUD → resize / center crop → normalize
Input tensor: 1 clip × 3 RGB channels × 16 frames × 256 × 256
3. Run frozen V-JEPA 2 ViT-L/16
Read activations after blocks 4, 12 and 24 separately
Each block: 8 temporal groups × 16 × 16 spatial tokens × 1,024 channels
4. Keep the last group; average across image space
16 × 16 tokens × 1,024 channels → 1,024 numbers
One vector per selected block. Channels are kept; only tokens are averaged.
The last group can use information from all 16 images through attention.
5. Fit a separate position readout for each block
1,024 numbers → ridge regression → estimated X, Z at t
Only this readout learns from coordinates. V-JEPA weights stay frozen.
6. Test on entire routes excluded from fitting
Compare estimated versus recorded position: error in blocks
CLOCK AND CONTEXT
16 images have 15 gaps.
15 × 0.4 s = 6 seconds.
No images later than t are used.
No memory carries between clips.
WHAT IS A TUBELET?
A token starts from a patch
16 × 16 pixels wide, over
2 consecutive frames.
16 input frames → 8 time groups.
Tokens mix information in the model.
SEPARATE COORDINATE PATH
Minecraft records X, Z
for the final image at t.
Training routes: fit the readout.
Held-out routes: score its error.
Coordinates never enter V-JEPA.
